children: Suja Life, the maker of organic cold-pressed juices and soft drinks, is seeing some weakness in the grocery aisle that led to it lowering its outlook, taking the fizz out of its stock.

Goldman Sachs analysts cut their rating on the stock to Neutral from Buy, with a $12 price target. Evercore ISI kept its Buy rating, but lowered its price target to $12, from $15 previously, according to FactSet. Jefferies analysts also kept their Buy rating, but lowered their price target to $17, from $22.
Suja shares closed down 12.9% at $8.68 on Wednesday.
Suja, whose brands include its namesake juice, Vive Organic wellness shots, and Slice soda, reported a wider-than-expected quarterly net loss of $8.3 million on revenue of $76.4 million on Tuesday.

Suja's loss of 22 cents a share was greater than the loss of 15 cents a share Wall Street was expecting. But revenue of $76.4 million increased 3.3% from a year earlier and came in above the $71.1 million expected.
Gross profit margin fell to 43.9% from 46.3% in the previous third quarter and 46.7% in the second quarter.

Investors may have especially focused on its full-year guidance for net sales of $351 million to $354 million, which would be up 7.5% to 8.4%, respectively, from its $326.6 million in fiscal 2025. The forecast was below its previous guidance of $360 million to $369 million, "reflecting current macroeconomic conditions and continued softness in the grocery channel," Suja said.

CEO Maria Stipp said Suja has gained market share in the natural healthy beverage category while most of the largest players in the category lost share. "Even with continued pressure in grocery, we're winning where shoppers are going, our newer lines are leading the way," she said.
The company expects adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization to rise roughly 70% this year, with margins expanding to nearly 20%, while investing in its brands.

Core net sales rose 3% in the quarter, driven by growth in cold-pressed juice, led by Refreshers, and continued growth in wellness shot multipacks, partially offset by softer single-serve shots and higher trade investment. Net sales of Emerging Brands rose 3%, despite slower-than-expected new distribution and "slower growth in the better-for-you soda category."
"With only about 11% of U.S. households buying our brands today, we see significant room to grow over the long term," Stipp added.
Suja said the revised guidance implies fourth-quarter net sales of $83.7 million to $86.7 million.

Suja now expects adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization of $68 million to $70 million, or 67.9% to 72.8% above its $40.5 million in the previous year. That, too, was down from its previous guidance for $70 million to $72 million.
